sources.citation: Energizer Homepower Installation Manual — https://www.energizersolar.com/s/22-11-11-Portal-Energizer-Homepower-Installation-Manual.pdf (downloaded to scratchpad/ez-hp.pdf)

transport: Vendor spec table lists supported communication as '2.4G Wi-Fi, RS 485, Ethernet, CTs' for the main unit and 'RS 485, CAN 2.0' for the battery link. The HP-6M carries an integrated comms module supporting Wi-Fi, 4G/LTE or Ethernet, one at a time. The RS-485 port runs Modbus RTU at 9600 baud, 8N1, slave ID 1. No register map or local endpoint is documented.
sharedMapEvidence: One installation manual covers HP-6M and HP-6S as a main/sub pair of the same series. The sub unit is a capacity extension of the main unit, not an independently addressed device, so 'shared map' is not really in play — but nothing about a register map is published for either.
gotchas: Cloud-dependent by design: the manual states the Installer App and the system must stay connected to the Energizer Homepower Cloud. Everything the user sees goes through that cloud. No local API is documented.
Rated energy 6.14 kWh per unit (5.8 kWh usable), up to 24.56 kWh with sub units. AC-coupled BESS, retrofits behind an existing PV system.
SAA-certified (Australia), country of manufacture China. Not a Canadian product.
